newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy pensions review needed in 1997 - Ciampi.
newsitem.headline: Italy pensions review needed in 1997 - Ciampi.

text.p: Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said in an interview published on Friday that a review of Italy's 1995 pension reform should be brought forward in 1997, instead of 1998 as planned.
"I still think we need to find a deal to bring it forward, in the interests of everyone," Ciampi told Il Sole 24 Ore financial daily.
"If we have to make corrections, why put it off until 1998 when the European game is up. Let's do it in 1997."
European Union states hoping to qualify to join a planned single currency at the start in 1999 will be judged on their economic credentials in early 1998, based on 1997 data.
Ciampi has already called for a review of the reforms signed by former technocrat prime minister Lamberto Dini as soon as possible to settle doubts about their effectiveness.

Unions have said they do not want the review to be brought forward, but employers' organisation Confindustria said earlier this month that without a swift overhaul of the reform, the government would not achieve its ambitious 1997 financial goals.
Employers argue that the reform introduces changes to Italy's heavily indebted state pensions' system too gradually and say the planned timetable for changes must be speeded up.
